definitions_and_conventions: Expectation E X is the Lebesgue integral of the real-valued random variable X on (Ω, Σ, P) [E2].
Variance is defined by Var(X) = E(X − E X)² [E1].
For p ∈ (0, ∞), ∥X∥Lp = (E|X|ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ, and Lp consists of the random variables for which this quantity is finite [E3–E4].
For p = 2, Equation (1.1) specializes the norm to ∥X∥L² = (E|X|²)¹ᐟ² [E5].
The notation σ(X) denotes the standard deviation; in the selected passage its value is identified as √(Var(X)), equivalently ∥X − E X∥L² [E6].
The source drops brackets around expectations and stipulates that nonlinear functions bind before expectation, so E(X − E X)² means the expectation of the squared centered random variable [E1–E2].
No representative/quotient convention is explicit: the text presents Lp elements as random variables X on Ω, even while calling Lp a vector space with a norm [E4, E7].

contract_plain_english: For a real-valued random variable X in the L² space of a probability space, the source says exactly that the L² norm of its centered version X − E X equals the square root of its variance and equals its standard deviation σ(X). Here Var(X) means E(X − E X)² and the L² norm comes from Equation (1.1). Membership in L² is inherited from the surrounding discussion rather than explicitly written in the identity sentence, and the passage does not explicitly choose between random-variable representatives and almost-sure-equivalence classes [E1–E7].
